[engine] A comparability stamp is only as behavioural as the gate that wrote it: once a gate stops testing presence and starts testing value, every sidecar produced under the old gate records an INTENT rather than an observation, so its knob values are unverifiable metadata. Decide the question with the measurement that is independent of the stamp -- bit-identical logits -- then repair the stamp; do not disarm the check with --allow-incomparable.

**class**: `gate-integrity`

## 為什麼（because）

ref_iq3_pool8gb_M2_6144_bitident.jsonl was dumped 2026-09-15 17:21 against the presence-based CGC_OA_ASYNC gate, so its .cap reads CGC_OA_ASYNC='0' even though that run used the segmented dispatcher -- at the time 0 and 1 selected the same branch because run_server.sh always exports the variable and the gate only asked whether it existed. After the 21:36 value-aware fix and the launcher default restored to 1, prefill250 resolved to 1 and the gate reported INVALID COMPARISON (ENV.CGC_OA_ASYNC: ref='0' now='1') on EVERY run, i.e. the comparability check that exists to prevent cross-config verdicts had gone dark for exactly the profile the gate runs under. The stamp was stale, not the run: M1 was 9/9 bit-identical against the old reference, and the non-segmented path lands on ff68c5a2 rather than the anchor dc055e63, so both sides provably ran the segmented path. Re-baselining produced a byte-identical dump (md5 d2f0b9a01fc5404ebb04dcf3583e133f for v2 and v3 alike), which is what makes correcting the sidecar a repair rather than a moved goalpost.
